context.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
context.conclusion: dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1, with E×[0,1]=F in the Euclidean space Eucl(n+1).

record.type: family, indexed by k∈ℕ, of Euclidean metric spaces
record.definition: Eucl(k)=ℝ^k, the real coordinate vectors indexed by {0,...,k−1}, with distance dist(x,y)=(∑_{j<k}(x_j−y_j)^2)^(1/2). Eucl(0) consists of the empty vector. On Eucl(k)×ℝ we use dist((x,t),(y,u))=(dist(x,y)^2+|t−u|^2)^(1/2), identified with Eucl(k+1) by appending the last coordinate; no maximum product metric is used. Balls mean {y:dist(x,y)<a}. All these spaces carry the topology of this metric and its Borel measurable structure.

record.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric or extended metric space
record.definition: For a subset A of a metric or extended metric space X, diam(A)=sup{d(x,y):x,y∈A} in [0,∞], where d is its (extended) distance and sup∅=0. Thus diam∅=0. When diam(A)≤a<∞ we treat it as the corresponding finite nonnegative real number. Countable sums of nonnegative quantities mean the supremum of finite partial sums, and may be infinite; powers with positive exponent have 0^s=0 and ∞^s=∞.

record.type: Hausdorff content and measure functions on Euclidean sets with positive real exponent
record.definition: For every k∈ℕ, A⊆Eucl(k), s>0 and δ>0, H^s_δ(A)=inf{∑_{i≥0}(diam U_i)^s : (U_i) is a countable cover of A and diam U_i≤δ for every i}, and H^s(A)=sup_{δ>0} H^s_δ(A), with values in [0,∞]. Finite covers are allowed by padding with empty sets; empty members contribute zero. The infimum of an empty collection is ∞. This is exactly the unnormalized diameter-power convention of problem.md:34–42.

record.type: pair of native Hausdorff measure and dimension constructions on an extended metric space
record.definition: For an extended metric space X with its Borel measurable structure, Native(X).measure(σ) denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure σ, defined in the pinned library as Measure.mkMetric(r↦r^σ). Here mkMetric forms, for each positive extended radius, the covering outer measure with cost r^σ of the extended diameter for nonempty sets (empty sets cost zero), and takes their supremum as the radius decreases to zero, with the Borel measure structure. Evaluations on arbitrary sets mean outer measure evaluations, without requiring those sets measurable. Extended powers use the native ENNReal.rpow convention, including r^0=1. Native(X).dimension(A) denotes dimH A, defined as sup over a∈[0,∞) with Native(X).measure(a)(A)=∞ of the extended nonnegative number a; an empty supremum is zero. This names the exact native definitions, not an assertion about H.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

record.type: extended nonnegative Hausdorff dimension of Euclidean sets
record.definition: For k∈ℕ and A⊆Eucl(k), dim_H(A)=Native(Eucl(k)).dimension(A), the usual Hausdorff dimension, valued in [0,∞]. In particular the empty set has dimension zero by this definition. No finiteness is imposed by this definition; finiteness of the dimensions occurring in the target is proved below.

I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}. When I or a subset of the real line is an argument of H or dim_H, it is identified with the subset of Eucl(1) obtained by t↦(t), the one-coordinate vector; this map has distance sqrt((t−u)^2)=|t−u|. Thus all diameter, cover and dimension notation for real subsets uses exactly their usual real-line metric. In λ(I) and real integrals I is the real interval itself.
F=E×I={(x,t):x∈E,t∈I}, regarded as a subset of Eucl(n+1) under D001's coordinate-appending Euclidean isometry.
D=dim_H(E). Finiteness and 0≤D≤n are conclusions, not assumptions.

record.type: Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line, evaluated as an outer measure on arbitrary sets
record.definition: λ is the usual Lebesgue measure MeasureTheory.volume on ℝ. For any nonnegative extended-real function f, ∫f dλ denotes its nonnegative Lebesgue integral (the supremum of the integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions bounded above by f). For a set B and constant c≥0, c 1_B is c on B and zero outside B. For a bounded open interval J=(a,b) with a<b its length |J| means b−a.

record.statement: For every extended metric space X, every measurable-space structure on X equal to its Borel structure, every real σ and every A⊆X, Native(X).measure(σ)(A)=sup_{r∈[0,∞],r>0} inf_{T:ℕ→Set(X), A⊆⋃_i T_i, ∀i diam(T_i)≤r} ∑_i sup_{T_i nonempty}(diam(T_i))^σ. The supremum over the nonemptiness proposition is the indicated power if T_i is nonempty and zero otherwise.

record.statement: For every k∈ℕ, A⊆Eucl(k), s>0 and δ>0: (i) H^s(A)=Native(Eucl(k)).measure(s)(A); (ii) dim_H(A)≥0, H^s(A)=0 if s>dim_H(A), and H^s(A)=∞ if 0<s<dim_H(A); conversely H^s(A)=0 implies dim_H(A)≤s, and H^s(A)=∞ implies dim_H(A)≥s. Also H^s_δ(A) is nonincreasing as δ increases. H^s(A)=0 implies that at every positive scale and every positive cost threshold there is an admissible countable cover with cost below that threshold. H^s(A)=∞ implies that for every L>0 and δ0>0 there exists 0<δ≤δ0 with H^s_δ(A)>L.

record.statement: E is bounded; there is R>0 with E⊆[−R,R]^n. For every s>0 and δ>0 there exists a finite cover of E by balls of diameter≤δ, of finite total s-cost; consequently H^s_δ(E)<∞. Also 0≤D≤n, so D is finite. If n=0 then E=Eucl(0) is a singleton and D=0.
